stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

All offices must comply to the new dress code starting next month.
hints: Some verbs always go with one fixed small word, such as to, with, on or in. Look at each verb and the small word after it.
Say the verb with its partner word: "comply to". Is that the standard pair in English?
Recall how this verb appears in formal memos and laws: "Employees must comply ___ the rules." Which small word fills the blank there? Compare it with the sentence, then check the other parts.

steps.action: Look at each verb and the preposition after it: "comply to".
steps.why: A preposition is a small linking word such as in, on, at, to, with or of.

steps.action: "Comply" always pairs with "with": comply with the rules.
steps.why: These pairs are fixed by usage, not by logic, so you have to memorize them.

steps.action: Check the other parts. "the new dress code" and "starting next month" are correct.
The error is "must comply to". It should be "must comply with".

trapNotes.the new dress code: This part is correct. A "dress code" is the set of rules on what to wear at work.
trapNotes.starting next month: This part is correct. "Starting next month" tells when the rule begins.
trapNotes.No error: "Comply to" is common in everyday Philippine English, so it may sound right. Standard English uses "comply with".
